name: Nebuzaradan
title: Chief of the Guard of Babylon
summary: Nebuzaradan was the commander of the guard for King Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon. He led the final destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC, exiled the people, but showed mercy to the prophet Jeremiah by setting him free.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Nebuzaradan led Babylonian forces in the final destruction of Jerusalem, including the burning of the temple, the royal palace, and all major buildings.

keyEvents.title: Plundering of the Temple
keyEvents.description: He oversaw the removal of all valuable items from the Lord's temple, including the bronze pillars, the basins, and all the gold and silver articles.

keyEvents.title: The Exile to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Nebuzaradan organized the deportation of Jerusalem's population to Babylon, but allowed some of the poorest to remain behind to tend the vineyards and fields.

keyEvents.title: Execution of Leaders at Riblah
keyEvents.description: He brought the priests, officials, and other leaders to King Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where they were executed.

keyEvents.title: The Release of Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: At Nebuchadnezzar's command, Nebuzaradan found the prophet Jeremiah in the prisoner camp and set him free, giving him the choice to go to Babylon or stay in the land.

keyEvents.title: Acknowledgment of God's Judgment
keyEvents.description: Nebuzaradan told Jeremiah that the Lord had brought this disaster upon the land because the people had sinned against their God.
